title: Design production auth users tenants and workspace model
final_sha_source_of_truth: GitHub issue comment after post-commit sync
missing_evidence: services/api/src/db/schema.js was listed in the issue brief, but the repository snapshot contains services/api/src/db/schema.sql instead.

model_summary.user_identity: Single canonical users table with provider-backed auth identities.
model_summary.tenant_model: Tenants are the top-level business container; memberships connect users to tenants.
model_summary.workspace_model: Workspaces are the operational boundary for files, search, wiki, jobs, and actions.
model_summary.role_model: RBAC with platform_admin, tenant_admin, workspace_admin, workspace_editor, workspace_viewer, agent_service, connector_runtime.
boundary_rules: Admins and clients remain separated in both data model and routes.
Agents/connectors act as service principals with narrow, auditable permissions.
Local client-agent access remains approval-gated and workspace-scoped.

migration_notes: Keep SQLite for the current local MVP while introducing PostgreSQL for production.
Use forward-only schema migrations and a default tenant/workspace backfill path.
Do not copy SQLite tables blindly; normalize them into workspace-scoped production tables.
Migrate identity and workspace ownership before moving the rest of the app data model.
route_boundary_impact: Add auth/session/invite routes for production identity.
Split admin, tenant, and workspace route groups.
Make provider settings and system controls admin-only.
Scope agent bridge and connector routes to explicit approvals and service principals.
immediate_next_task: Implement PostgreSQL-backed identity, tenant, workspace, and membership tables plus request-context middleware, then refactor the highest-risk admin-only route groups to consume workspace-scoped authorization.
notes: This task is design-and-schema planning only.
No runtime auth changes were implemented in this pass.
